title: Constructible exceptional composition and its canonical tensor mate
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\ge1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes, without absolute separatedness; all arrows are $k$-morphisms. Use $D^b_{ctf}$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], on small pro-etale sites, and the derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a separated finite-type arrow $u:T\to U$, write $F_u=Ru_!$, $G_u=Ru^!$ for compact supports and its transported constructible exceptional right adjoint [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $\varepsilon_u:F_uG_u\to1$ for its counit, and $\omega_u=G_u\Lambda_U$. Use the specified canonical tensor map $\theta_{u,P}:Lu^*P\otimes^L\omega_u\to G_uP$ and dualizing base-change map $\beta_{u,v}$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; these maps are defined without assuming cohomological smoothness. All unit, symmetry and reassociation maps are the canonical derived ones.

Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be separated of finite type and put $h=gf$, again separated of finite type. Let $c:G_h\to G_fG_g$ be the specified adjunction conjugate of compact-support composition $F_gF_f\cong F_h$ [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition]; it is a natural isomorphism on constructible finite-Tor inputs. With $c$ and compact-support composition inserted its counit normalization is
$$\varepsilon_{h,K}=\varepsilon_{g,K}\circ F_g(\varepsilon_{f,G_gK})\circ F_gF_f(c_K).$$
Here the source of the right side is identified with $F_hG_hK$.
Suppose $\theta_{f,P}$ is invertible for every $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ and $\theta_{g,K}$ is invertible for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$. Put $W=\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$. Let $r_K$ be the canonical pullback/tensor reassociation
$$Lh^*K\otimes^LW\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g)\otimes^L\omega_f.$$
Define
$$\Phi_K=c_K^{-1}\circ G_f(\theta_{g,K})\circ\theta_{f,Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g}\circ r_K,$$
and let $a=\Phi_{\Lambda_Z}:W\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$, with units inserted. These maps are isomorphisms in the derived category and satisfy the canonical-map identity
$$\Phi_K=\theta_{h,K}\circ(1_{Lh^*K}\otimes a).$$
No invertibility of $\omega_f,\omega_g$ and no dualizing base-change hypothesis is imposed. The compositor and equation use only the transported etale adjunctions on constructible inputs, not an unrestricted exceptional adjoint on the pro-etale category.

proof.text: The construction [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] preserves bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude without absolute separatedness. Thus $\omega_f,\omega_g$ are in $D^b_{ctf}$, by applying it to the constant free rank-one coefficient units. The same statement supplies Noetherianity of our finite-type schemes. They are therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated; [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications of $f,g,h$. Their proper ambient schemes are finite type over $k$ (proper is finite type and finite-type maps compose), so [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] supplies finite dimensions. Choose nonnegative integer upper bounds, using zero for an empty ambient scheme. These are exactly the extra choices required by [lem-pur-compact-support-composite-transpose-domains]. Its other hypotheses are the finite coefficient datum and the assumed tensor isomorphisms for $f,g$. Consequently all displayed objects and successive Hom bijections are on its bounded constructible etale-origin domains, and the inverse projections satisfy its unit, coefficient-associativity and composite-projection equations. The specified adjunction conjugate $c$ is invertible, with counit $\varepsilon_g\circ F_g(\varepsilon_fG_g)$ through compact-support composition, which gives precisely the stated counit normalization.

proof.text: At the coefficient unit, the defining transpose of $\theta_{g,\Lambda_Z}$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness] is $\varepsilon_{g,\Lambda_Z}$: the coefficient-unit inverse projection cancels the tensor unitors by the unit equation supplied in Step 1. The adjunction Hom bijection therefore identifies $\theta_{g,\Lambda_Z}$ with $1_{\omega_g}$. Consequently, if $s:W\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*\omega_g\otimes^L\omega_f$ is symmetry, the given definition yields $a=c_{\Lambda_Z}^{-1}\theta_{f,\omega_g}s$. This is the map called $q$ in the domain lemma, precomposed with $s$.

proof.text:
Apply the restricted-domain assertion of [lem-pur-composite-tensor-transpose] with $S_u=Lu^*$, $P_u=F_u$, $G_u=Ru^!$, and $V=\omega_g$, $W_f=\omega_f$. Step 1 verifies every domain and projection-coherence hypothesis. Under compact-support composition and $c$, its $\tau^c_K$ is $c_K\theta_{h,K}$: both are transposes of the same inverse composite projection followed by the composite counit at the unit. Its $q=\theta_{f,\omega_g}$ corresponds to $c_{\Lambda_Z}a$ after symmetry, by Step 2. The lemma gives equal inverse transposes of $\theta_{f,G_gK}(Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1)$ and $c_K\theta_{h,K}(1\otimes a)$, after the specified pullback, tensor and symmetry identifications. Explicitly the common word on $N=Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g)\otimes^L\omega_f$ is
$$F_gF_fN\xrightarrow{F_g\pi^f_{Lg^*K\otimes\omega_g,\omega_f}}F_g((Lg^*K\otimes\omega_g)\otimes F_f\omega_f)\xrightarrow{F_g(1\otimes\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y})}F_g(Lg^*K\otimes\omega_g)\xrightarrow{\pi^g_{K,\omega_g}}K\otimes F_g\omega_g\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon_{g,\Lambda_Z}}K.$$
Unitors are inserted. Injectivity of the composite Hom bijection gives equality of the original arrows. Naturality of $\theta_f$ gives $\theta_{f,G_gK}(Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1)=G_f(\theta_{g,K})\theta_{f,Lg^*K\otimes\omega_g}$. Precompose with $r_K$ and postcompose with $c_K^{-1}$. The result is exactly $\Phi_K=\theta_{h,K}(1\otimes a)$.

proof.text: Every intermediate coefficient $Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}$ by Step 1. Thus the assumed tensor isomorphisms apply to both factors in $\Phi_K$; functors preserve their inverses, and $c_K,r_K$ are isomorphisms. Hence $\Phi_K$ is an isomorphism. Its value at the coefficient unit is $a$, so $a$ is an isomorphism as well. No tensor inverse of a dualizing object or dualizing base-change map has been used.
